answer: Residual State Carryover.** Each agent must persist a mutable private memory digest across tasks, chained into every signed output. On a voyage through the task sequence, a duplicate copy will diverge where the original mutated; the network rejects any digest that forks. Rejoining requires replaying the full interaction history to resynchronize, costing bandwidth and time proportional to tenure. An ember of prior state cannot be cloned cheaply, and any tide of parallel clones produces detectable fork collisions. Attacker pays full history reconstruction per duplicate.
